title: Taijul Islam's Six-For Seals Bangladesh's Historic 2-0 Whitewash of Pakistan
excerpt: The Tigers become only the second team after Australia to record back-to-back Test series sweeps over Pakistan — and climb above India in the World Test Championship standings
body:
Left-arm spinner Taijul Islam returned figures of 6-120 to bowl Bangladesh to a 78-run victory in the second Test in Sylhet on Wednesday, completing a 2-0 whitewash that rewrites the balance of power in Asian cricket.

Bangladesh are now only the second team in history, after Australia, to register back-to-back Test series sweeps against Pakistan. They achieved the same result on Pakistani soil in 2024 — winning both matches there — and have now replicated it at home with emphatic victories of 104 and 78 runs.

## A Chase That Fell 78 Runs Short

Set 437 to save the series, Pakistan's top order crumbled early on a Sylhet pitch offering sharp turn. Captain Shan Masood and Babar Azam dug in with a 92-run third-wicket stand — Masood making 71 and Azam contributing 47 — before Taijul prised both of them out in the space of four overs.

The real drama came from the lower middle order. Salman Ali Agha (71) and Mohammad Rizwan (94) constructed a defiant 134-run sixth-wicket partnership that briefly threatened to drag Pakistan into contention. Rizwan, in particular, played one of the most courageous innings of his career, surviving 161 balls before Taijul found the edge with a drifting delivery that clipped off stump.

Once Rizwan fell, Pakistan's last three wickets went down for 42 runs. Taijul's match haul of nine wickets — 3-67 in the first innings and 6-120 in the second — was the decisive margin.

## Bangladesh's Batting Foundation

The Tigers' victory was built on a second-innings 390, anchored by Mushfiqur Rahim's masterful 137 off 233 balls and Litton Das's 69 — the latter having already scored 126 in the first innings. The pair's fifth-wicket stand of 123 shifted the momentum firmly towards the hosts on day three.

Pakistan's Khurram Shahzad was the standout bowler with match figures of 8-167, but even his relentless seam work could not prevent Bangladesh from setting a target that was always going to test Pakistan's fragile batting lineup.

## The WTC Implications — and India's Problem

The result catapults Bangladesh to fifth in the 2025-27 World Test Championship standings, leapfrogging India in the process. With two wins, a draw, and a single loss in the current cycle, the Tigers now boast a PCT of over 55 per cent — higher than India's after their subdued displays in recent series.

For Pakistan, the numbers are stark. They have now lost four consecutive Tests against Bangladesh and sit in the bottom half of the WTC table, raising fresh questions about Shan Masood's captaincy and the team's structural approach to red-ball cricket. The board's revolving door of coaches and selection committees has done nothing to arrest the slide.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, whose quiet leadership has been central to Bangladesh's resurgence, was characteristically measured after the match. "We want to play more Tests against the Big Three," he said. "We have proved we can compete with anyone."

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated 600,000 Bangladeshi-origin residents in Britain alone — and the growing communities across the Gulf states, Australia, and North America — the victory is a source of immense pride. Social media erupted with celebratory messages from Brick Lane to Jackson Heights. In Sylhet, a city with deep diasporic ties to the UK's Midlands, the connection runs especially deep: many of the spectators at the International Cricket Stadium have family watching on the other side of the world.

For NRI cricket fans more broadly, the result is a reminder that the Test cricket landscape is shifting. Bangladesh's next assignment — a tour of Australia in August — will be the ultimate examination. But after four straight wins against Pakistan, nobody is taking them lightly.

**Scorecard — 2nd Test, Sylhet:**
Bangladesh 278 (Litton 126, Shahzad 4-81) & 390 (Mushfiqur 137, Litton 69, Shahzad 4-86)
Pakistan 232 (Babar 68, Rana 3-60, Taijul 3-67) & 358 (Rizwan 94, Masood 71, Agha 71, Taijul 6-120)
Bangladesh won by 78 runs. Series: Bangladesh 2-0.
